package_info.package_versions: unknown (all versions distributed during the SmoothOperator campaign)
package_info.why_malicious: The 3CXDesktopApp installer was trojanized in a supply chain attack, resulting in the distribution of a malicious DLL (such as ffmpeg.dll or d3dcompiler_47.dll) that is loaded by the application at runtime. This DLL establishes communication with attacker-controlled infrastructure, enabling remote command execution, data exfiltration, and further compromise of affected systems.

execution_context.file_location: 3CXDesktopApp installation directory, malicious DLL (e.g., ffmpeg.dll or d3dcompiler_47.dll)
required_permissions: filesystem (read/write for persistence or data collection)
process (ability to spawn or inject into other processes)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At application startup, the code collects system information and sends it via HTTPS POST to a hardcoded attacker-controlled domain, then receives and executes remote commands, enabling remote control and data exfiltration.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The DLL initiates outbound network connections to attacker-controlled infrastructure and executes code received from the network, which is not expected behavior for legitimate multimedia or system DLLs.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate DLLs loaded by 3CXDesktopApp should only provide expected multimedia or system functionality and should not initiate network communications to external, non-3CX domains or execute arbitrary remote commands.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Some legitimate applications may check for updates or contact vendor servers, but they do not execute arbitrary code received from untrusted sources or communicate with unknown external domains.
key_indicators: Outbound HTTPS POST requests from 3CXDesktopApp or its DLLs to non-3CX domains
Collection and exfiltration of system information at application startup
Dynamic execution of code or commands received from remote servers
Presence of modified or unsigned DLLs (ffmpeg.dll, d3dcompiler_47.dll) in the application directory

attack_chain.action: User downloads and installs the trojanized 3CXDesktopApp containing a malicious DLL (e.g., ffmpeg.dll or d3dcompiler_47.dll).
attack_chain.leads_to: Malicious DLL is present in the application directory and will be loaded at application startup.

attack_chain.action: Malicious DLL is loaded by the 3CXDesktopApp at runtime when the application is launched.
attack_chain.leads_to: Malicious code is executed within the context of the 3CXDesktopApp process.

attack_chain.action: Malicious code collects system information and sends it to the attacker's C2 server via HTTPS POST.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker receives system information and can issue further commands to the infected system.

attack_chain.action: Attacker sends commands to the infected system, which are received and executed by the malicious code.
attack_chain.leads_to: Remote control, data theft, or further compromise of the affected system.

behavioral_signatures: Unexpected outbound HTTPS connections from 3CXDesktopApp or its loaded DLLs to non-3CX domains
DLLs loaded by 3CXDesktopApp initiating network beacons or POST requests at application startup
Execution of code or commands received from remote servers by 3CXDesktopApp processes
file_indicators: Presence of ffmpeg.dll or d3dcompiler_47.dll with unexpected hashes or missing/invalid digital signatures in the 3CXDesktopApp installation directory
Unknown or modified DLLs appearing in the 3CXDesktopApp directory that do not match official vendor releases
network_indicators: Outbound connections from 3CXDesktopApp to attacker-controlled C2 domains (e.g., hardcoded beacon URLs such as https://attacker-c2.com/beacon)
Unusual HTTPS POST requests originating from 3CXDesktopApp processes to domains not associated with 3CX
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor 3CXDesktopApp and its loaded DLLs for unexpected outbound network activity, especially HTTPS POST requests to domains not associated with 3CX. Verify the integrity and digital signatures of DLLs in the application directory against known-good hashes. Flag any process spawning or code execution initiated by these DLLs, and correlate observed network destinations with known C2 infrastructure.
